script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Tuesday, November 24. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 10 degrees Celsius, clear skies. The high will be 19 and the low 9 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 0 percent.

You have 2 appointments in the next 24 hours: 3:00 PM, Financial issues capillary line; 4:00 PM, Meeting with Mr. Abshahi.

Now, the top 5 stories in AI today.

First, from The Verge: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang. After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A.

Second, from The Verge: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next? After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation.

Third, from The Verge: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang. I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.

Fourth, from TechCrunch: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes. As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.

Fifth, from TechCrunch: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios. Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
